system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Incomplete figure on a grid]

The squares in the grid above have areas of 1 square centimeter. Draw lines to complete the figure so that it has an area of 13 square centimeters.

Figure, described in words:
A grid measuring 8 squares wide and 6 squares high. At the bottom right of the grid, a single square cell is indicated with dimension arrows showing a width of '1 cm' and a height of '1 cm'. An incomplete polygon is drawn with heavy black lines on the grid intersections:
- A horizontal segment 4 units long on the 1st horizontal line from the top, extending from column 1 to column 5 (where grid lines are numbered 0 to 8 horizontally, and 0 to 6 vertically).
- From the point (1, 1), a diagonal segment runs down and right 2 units horizontally and 2 units vertically to (3, 3).
- From (3, 3), a vertical segment runs down 2 units to (3, 5).
- From (3, 5), a horizontal segment runs right 2 units to (5, 5).
The points (5, 1) and (5, 5) are currently open endpoints.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw a line from the open endpoint (5, 1) straight right 3 units along the top grid line to (8, 1). From (8, 1) draw a line straight down 1 unit to (8, 2). From (8, 2) draw a line straight left 3 units to (5, 2). From (5, 2) draw a line straight down 3 units to (5, 5), which closes the figure at the open endpoint (5, 5). The completed figure is the polygon (1,1), (8,1), (8,2), (5,2), (5,5), (3,5), (3,3). It consists of the original 10 square centimeter region plus a 3 by 1 rectangle of 3 square centimeters on the right, so its area is 10 + 3 = 13 square centimeters.
